<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AOGMPhCQP/softphone-network-requirements-does-every-zia-customer-in-the-world-bypass-5060-and-5061","lastmod":"2024-04-01T16:15:56.000Z","id":"0D54u0000AOGMPhCQP"} -->
## Softphone network requirements... Does every ZIA customer in the world bypass :5060 and :5061?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AOGMPhCQP/softphone-network-requirements-does-every-zia-customer-in-the-world-bypass-5060-and-5061
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-03-27T18:11:34.000Z
- Last activity: 2024-04-01T16:15:56.000Z
- Answers: 4
- Likes: 0
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p><span style="font-size: 14px;">Been a while since I checked in here...!</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">I have provisioned several different softphones through ZIA but I am hitting a wall here with </span><strong style="font-size: 14px;">ServiceTitan Phones Pro</strong><span style="font-size: 14px;">. I don't generally rush into Zscaler Support cases because, in my experience, the focus is always 'how quickly can we bypass this traffic' instead of properly handle it with any of the tools available to us such as URL and Cloud App Control, Firewall Control, etc. This time, I find myself opening a support case and in the support reps defense we did troubleshoot the connectivity and they were also confused as to why my configurations were not working. Unfortunately, I do not have a TAM to communicate with but that's just the way the cookie crumbles for me.</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">After 2 hours of troubleshooting together, we collected to ZCC packet captures and I provided to the case.</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">Support suggested that I add "0.0.0.0/0:5060" &amp; "0.0.0.0/0:5061" to destination exclusions at the policy level therefore completely bypassing the SIP requirements for the soft phone network requirements. Prior to bypassing 5060&amp;5061 the only part of the connectivity test that was failing was the Firewall requirements for ports between 16384-32768. After bypassing 5060&amp;5061, I am now failing the SIP requirements of the test as well...</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">Support also provided this link.</span></p><p><a href="https://help.zscaler.com/zia/zia-and-application-layer-gateway-enabled-applications#:~:text=Protocols%20that%20are%20not%20supported,your%20GRE%20or%20IPSec%20tunnel." rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-size: 14px;">ZIA &amp; Application Layer Gateway Enabled Applications | Zscaler</a></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">"</span><strong style="font-size: 14px;">Protocols that are not supported (like SIP, H.323, H.248, VOIP, and TFTP) should be bypassed from Zscaler by changing the configuration on the firewall or router when configuring your GRE or IPSec tunnel.</strong><span style="font-size: 14px;">"</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">To me, that document suggests either of the two options. Zscaler bake the bypass of unsupported protocols into their own application. Or produce a process allowlist of everything that </span><strong style="font-size: 14px;">needs</strong><span style="font-size: 14px;"> to be bypassed similar to the below document? Or maybe there is one and I just haven't found it...</span></p><p><a href="https://help.zscaler.com/zia/certificate-pinning-and-ssl-inspection" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Certificate Pinning and SSL Inspection | Zscaler</a></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">What I am trying to accomplish seems fairly simple compared to other soft phones... Going to scrap what I have and start from scratch again while waiting for the next support update. Of course, the moment I disable ZIA, the test succeeds in "Firewall Ports" and then fails in VOIP and SIP where it would succeed through ZIA until I bypassed SIP at a policy level.</span></p><p><br></p><p><a href="https://help.servicetitan.com/how-to/how-to-phones-pro-network-recommendations" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-size: 14px;">Phones Pro network recommendations and setup (servicetitan.com)</a></p><p><a href="https://servicetitan.visualware.com/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">ServiceTitan Network Test (visualware.com)</a></p>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000ASPQhcCQH/managing-the-quic-protocol","lastmod":"2024-09-02T05:47:39.000Z","id":"0D54u0000ASPQhcCQH"} -->
## Managing the QUIC Protocol

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000ASPQhcCQH/managing-the-quic-protocol
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-05-06T13:34:23.000Z
- Last activity: 2024-09-02T05:47:39.000Z
- Answers: 6
- Likes: 2
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p>Wanting to start this thread and check to see what other Zscaler Internet Acces Customers are doing.</p><p><br></p><p>Recently, I have been getting upticks in browser latency reports and I have been able to replicate the experience on multiple workstations where I can generate anywhere of 10-60 seconds between clicks with ZIA enabled. I also noticed a commonality between my traffic and all the users reporting the issue. More QUIC traffic... I am looking for information in Chromium Org where they suggest they are optimizing their QUIC protocol or making changes to how much traffic is pumped through that protocol, but I don't see much.</p><p><br></p><p>So, as it is already blocked and I am doing what the <a href="https://help.zscaler.com/zia/managing-quic-protocol?_bt=&amp;_bk=&amp;_bm=&amp;_bn=x&amp;_bg=&amp;utm_source=google&amp;utm_medium=cpc&amp;utm_campaign=google-ads-na&amp;gad_source=1&amp;gclid=EAIaIQobChMIjMbunor5hQMVPJXCCB3Z3gUIEAAYASAAEgLVmPD_BwE" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Managing the QUIC Protocol | Zscaler</a> article says to try first I looked for other options. I noticed we didn't have a policy around QUIC within Intune and I stood up some test policies to disable QUIC at the browser level. This should force revert all the QUIC traffic to standard TCP and then be delivered much better to the end user in the browser. So far that is the experience, and I will be sending all reports this direction so that I can make a planned effort to change this for all soon.</p><p><br></p><p>However, Zscaler Support told me to call my ISP... As they commonly do when I can generate Latency or open latency related tickets. This didn't make a lot of sense being that I could replicate the latency on Edge &amp; Chrome, but Firefox was just fine... I find it weird that support always treats me as if we are the only customer in the world that has the latency issues. I wanted to see if any others have been having latency reports for the last 2-3 months this year. I want to say my earliest report was a single user back in January/February time frame, but I have been able to basically classify this as an org wide issue at this point as I measured the "proxy latency" across my organization for a 24hr period and the average latency was 10.63+ seconds rather than milliseconds...</p><p><br></p><p>The process I am taking with end users for the time being is below.</p><p><br></p><p>Windows Workstation</p><p>Chrome Browser</p><ol><li><span style="font-size: inherit;">navigate to "chrome://flags"</span></li><li><span style="font-size: inherit;">search for "quic" (experimental quic protocol)</span></li><li><span style="font-size: inherit;">select the drop down that states "default" and select "disabled"</span></li></ol><p>Edge Browser</p><ol><li><span style="font-size: inherit;">navigate to "edge://flags"</span></li><li><span style="font-size: inherit;">search for "quic" (experimental quic protocol)</span></li><li><span style="font-size: inherit;">select the drop down that states "default" and select "disabled"</span></li></ol><p>MacOS workstations</p><ol><li><span style="font-size: inherit;">open the Terminal from Applications > Utilities folder</span></li><li><span style="font-size: inherit;">enter the below command</span><ol><li><span style="font-size: inherit;">defaults write com.google.Chrome LegacyTLSEnforcedNegotiationPolicy -bool true</span></li></ol></li></ol><p><br></p>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

---

## Failed Client SSL Handshake

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000ASQTuBCQX/failed-client-ssl-handshake
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-05-08T12:08:25.000Z
- Last activity: 2025-09-03T12:06:13.000Z
- Answers: 7
- Likes: 0
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p>Occasionally, I get an error with a page that has an issue with SSL handshake processing. Typically this manifests itself in the logs as a Policy Action error with the message "Dropped due to failed client SSL handshake". I can enable additional fields in the Web Log viewer like "Client SSL Handshake Failure Reason" however, this information is inadequate to say the least. This leaves my only recourse to create an SSL Bypass rule and I am kind of tired of that being the only solution without a decent reason to justify it. As an example, googleapis.com hosts some content in a core CSS for one of our highly used resources on the web. Again, I got the "Dropped due to failed client SSL handshake" and the only reason I could discern from the "Client SSL Handshake Failure Reason" was "Close Notify or Client TCP Reset". This is not adequate. What was the negotiation error? Was there no ciphers available for client and server to agree upon? If so, state that. Show me the offered ciphers and protocol, show me what the Zscaler cloud accepts. I assume the handshake failure is coming from the negotiation of the connection between the GoogleAPIs.com host and the Zscaler Cloud because if I bypass ZIA, the client connection from browser to GoogleAPIs.com works fine.</p><p><br></p><p>How can I help myself out with this besides creating an SSL bypass rule/policy? What SSL/TLS protocols and Cipher suites does the Zscaler Cloud allow/accept to negotiate on? How do I get more information to address issues like this?</p>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AUjnbCCQR/atlassian-zscaler-zia-best-practices-for-http2-part-1","lastmod":"2024-06-05T02:30:46.000Z","id":"0D54u0000AUjnbCCQR"} -->
## Atlassian & Zscaler ZIA Best Practices for HTTP2 - Part 1

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AUjnbCCQR/atlassian-zscaler-zia-best-practices-for-http2-part-1
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-06-04T23:47:06.000Z
- Last activity: 2024-06-05T02:30:46.000Z
- Answers: 0
- Likes: 0
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">This article outlines how best to configure Zscaler ZIA in order to provide the best user experience to users of Atlassian products. This document should be used as a companion guide to the </span><a href="https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-technology-partners/zscaler-and-atlassian-deployment-guide" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"><u>Zscaler and Atlassian Deployment Guide</u></a><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">, which outlines how Zscaler should be deployed with Atlassian for Zscaler ZIA, ZPA and ZPC.</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">This guide is for network administrators, endpoint / IT administrators, and security analysts responsible for deploying, monitoring, and managing enterprise security systems. For additional product and company resources, refer to:</span></p><ul><li><a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Tf5s7fot5DfzQNISI6MxO5wXPFu2oolnLmo0rcE9zCw/edit#heading=h.bx9d7nfugz0a" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-size: 12pt;"><u>Zscaler Resources</u></a></li><li><a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Tf5s7fot5DfzQNISI6MxO5wXPFu2oolnLmo0rcE9zCw/edit#heading=h.eilwq1byk9uw" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-size: 12pt;"><u>Atlassian Resources</u></a></li><li><a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Tf5s7fot5DfzQNISI6MxO5wXPFu2oolnLmo0rcE9zCw/edit#heading=h.am81bwczejpo" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-size: 12pt;"><u>Appendix A: Requesting Zscaler Support</u></a></li><li><a href="https://support.atlassian.com/organization-administration/docs/ip-addresses-and-domains-for-atlassian-cloud-products/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"><u>IP addresses and domains for Atlassian cloud products</u></a></li></ul><p><br></p><h3><strong style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 14pt;">Software Versions</strong></h3><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">This article was authored using ZIA v6.2 (as of May 2024) and Atlassian Production Release, current as of May 2024. An Atlassian free tier account was used to create and verify the features enabled and used as examples. Create an </span><a href="https://www.atlassian.com/software/free" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"><u>Atlassian Free Account</u></a><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">. Click Log in, then select Sign up for an account.</span></p><p><br></p><h2><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 18pt;">Zscaler and HTTP/2</span></h2><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Zscaler supports inspection of HTTP traffic using the </span><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application-Layer_Protocol_Negotiation" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"><u>ALPN</u></a><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"> protocol (Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation). ALPN is an extension of TLS which allows for negotiation of HTTP connections in the most efficient way. It has now become common for SaaS applications and web servers to offer HTTP/2(as well as HTTP/1.1) as part of the ALPN protocol negotiation to enhance users' experience of web applications.</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">In 2023, Zscaler added support for </span><a href="https://help.zscaler.com/zia/release-upgrade-summary-2023" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"><u>SSL inspection of the HTTP/2 protocol</u></a><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"> for web and non web traffic. However, by default, this feature is not enabled by default and must be explicitly enabled by the Zscaler ZIA Administrator through Zscaler support.&nbsp;</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">If a web server presents HTTP/2 as a connection option, Zscaler ZIA will always choose HTTP/1.1 for that connection with the default settings.&nbsp;</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">For some web applications, forcing HTTP connections to HTTP/1.1(Instead of HTTP/2) can impact the user experience. Therefore, it is recommended to enable HTTP/2 inspection in order to provide the best user experience.&nbsp;</span></p><p><br></p><h2><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 18pt;">Configuring Zscaler ZIA SSL Inspection Policy for HTTP/2</span></h2><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">If your Zscaler ZIA tenant is not enabled for HTTP/2 inspection, it can be enabled by opening a support ticket and requesting it be enabled. Once HTTP/2 is enabled for your tenant, a selection dialog becomes available in SSL Inspection Policy settings called ‘Enable HTTP/2’:</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Policy>SSL Inspection</span></p><p><br></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iCbSL?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Edit a new or existing SSL Inspection Policy:</span></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iCbSf?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">HTTP/2 will need to be enabled for all policies which need it.</span></p><p><br></p><p>Loom Video:</p><h2><a href="https://www.loom.com/share/15db2bf2a132494bab99fe8131c045c5?sid=c8b53065-24c5-4896-8b87-e16da84caf72" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">How to enable HTTP/2 in your ZIA tenant</a></h2>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AUjneJCQR/atlassian-zscaler-zia-best-practices-for-http2-part-2","lastmod":"2026-05-28T23:14:36.000Z","id":"0D54u0000AUjneJCQR"} -->
## Atlassian & Zscaler ZIA Best Practices for HTTP2 - Part 2

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AUjneJCQR/atlassian-zscaler-zia-best-practices-for-http2-part-2
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-06-04T23:50:51.000Z
- Last activity: 2026-05-28T23:14:36.000Z
- Answers: 0
- Likes: 2
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<h2><strong style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 18pt;">How best to configure SSL Inspection policy for Atlassian services</strong></h2><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">In some cases, you may want to be more explicit with your SSL inspection policies. In this case, defining the explicit destinations may be required. Atlassian documents these URLs here: </span><a href="https://support.atlassian.com/organization-administration/docs/ip-addresses-and-domains-for-atlassian-cloud-products/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"><u>IP addresses and domains for Atlassian cloud products</u></a><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">. In order to do this for Atlassian you would need to do the following:</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Define Atlassian URL’s which need to be defined in policy:</span></p><ol><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Create a new custom URL Category Administration>URL Categories</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Click ‘Add URL Category’</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Populate the form as below with the following domains:</span></li></ol><p><br></p><p class="ql-indent-2"><strong style="font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;, monospace; font-size: 9pt;"><em>.atlassian.net</em></strong></p><p class="ql-indent-2"><strong style="font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;, monospace; font-size: 9pt;"><em>.atlassian.com</em></strong></p><p class="ql-indent-2"><strong style="font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;, monospace; font-size: 9pt;"><em>.trello.com</em></strong></p><p class="ql-indent-2"><strong style="font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;, monospace; font-size: 9pt;"><em>.bitbucket.org</em></strong></p><p class="ql-indent-2"><strong style="font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;, monospace; font-size: 9pt;"><em>.atl-paas.net</em></strong></p><p class="ql-indent-2"><strong style="font-family: &quot;Courier New&quot;, monospace; font-size: 9pt;"><em>.jira.com</em></strong></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Note:&nbsp;</span></p><ul><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">The preceding ‘.’ is important as it indicates a wildcard for all domains/sub-domains that match.</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">If you are using custom domains for your Atlassian services, make sure you add them to this list.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">You can also add the explicit first party domains from Atlassian that you may be using such as </span><a href="https://nscaler.atlassian.net/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-family: NTR, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"><u>https://nscaler.atlassian.net</u></a></li></ul><p><br></p><ol><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Click Save and navigate to Policy>SSL Inspection</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Click Add SSL Inspection Rule and do the following:</span><ol><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Adjust the Rule Order to match your tenant requirements</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Specify the rule name</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Select the URL Categories dropdown and select the URL Category you created called ‘Atlassian Cloud Service URLs’</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Enable the HTTP/2 toggle</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Save</span></li></ol></li><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Apply and Activate the policy changes, attempt to generate some traffic towards the Atlassian services you are using</span></li></ol><p><br></p><h2><strong style="font-size: 18pt; font-family: NTR, sans-serif;">How to view logs in Webview and confirm HTTP/2 inspection is taking place</strong></h2><p><br></p><ol><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Then navigate the Web Insight logs and create a filter matching:</span><ol><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">Current time period</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">ALPN Protocol: HTTP/2 over TLS</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">URL Search: Domain matching ‘atlassian’. You should see HTTP/2 transactions</span></li></ol></li></ol><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iCbSk?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p>Loom Video:</p><p><a href="https://www.loom.com/share/9d1a97c7b29d442dbc4490ccff24851c?sid=594aa105-1cfb-4d70-a6d6-ae044057782b" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">How to create a specific SSL Policy for Atlassian URLs with HTTP/2</a></p>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AXRTC5CQP/managine-quic-v2-webview2dll-embedded-browser-functionality-not-respecting-browser-control","lastmod":"2025-01-23T21:08:59.000Z","id":"0D54u0000AXRTC5CQP"} -->
## Managine QUIC v2! WebView2.dll (embedded browser functionality not respecting browser control)

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AXRTC5CQP/managine-quic-v2-webview2dll-embedded-browser-functionality-not-respecting-browser-control
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-07-10T19:49:09.000Z
- Last activity: 2025-01-23T21:08:59.000Z
- Answers: 10
- Likes: 4
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p>Here we go again......!</p><p><br></p><p>My last post was around the latency our organization was experiencing on our managed browsers with the QUIC protocol since Chromium updates late last year. We resolved these issues by following <em>Alternative</em> method as the initial blocking of QUIC on ZIA-FW was no longer functioning properly. Once we disabled QUIC on the browsers the issues were resolved.</p><p><br></p><p>Around the time we disabled QUIC on the browsers we started noticing sporadic latency reports around Teams, Outlook, CyberArk's PSMConnectionMgr.exe Application, and more. </p><p><br></p><p>While investigating this latency we did troubleshot extensively and noticed that WebView2.dll was a common factor in all the reports. As WebView2.dll embeds browser functionality into applications it is somewhat difficult to monitor this traffic through ZCC pcaps as the app would fail from Tunnel2.0 to 1.0 and then send all the data as application data. After adding some additional filters to the pcaps we noticed that all the Application Data was piping out UDP/443 traffic (QUIC!!!). </p><p><br></p><p>We tested many different configurations around this and there was no resolution identified for the Latency. I opened a case with Zscaler support(<span style="font-size: 14px; font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI Web (West European)&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Roboto, &quot;Helvetica Neue&quot;, sans-serif;">Case Number : 04913822). We did a lot of the same troubleshooting as well as some additional testing with through the escalation process. We(org side) stumbled upon the below documentation and eventually added a regedit key to disable QUIC for WebView2 and resolved countless latency issues with applications.</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px; font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI Web (West European)&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Roboto, &quot;Helvetica Neue&quot;, sans-serif;">The part that is troublesome here is our sr management doesn't latch on to org-wide changes that we test, validate, and deploy when there is no official documentation that suggests the change is needed. I have requested through the case that Zscaler update documentation around WebView2.dll and managing the QUIC protocol but they seem very hesitant as "</span><span style="font-size: 15px; font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI Web (West European)&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Roboto, &quot;Helvetica Neue&quot;, sans-serif;">As we do not have any known or global issue found with webview2 and&nbsp;Microsoft&nbsp;&nbsp;or CyberArk ." This is a troubling response, if we did not have ZIA we would not have ever needed this control around the QUIC protocol. If we weren't following the doc on managing QUIC protocol by blocking it from the browsers, we likely never would have seen these issues across our org.</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 15px; font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI Web (West European)&quot;, &quot;Segoe UI&quot;, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Roboto, &quot;Helvetica Neue&quot;, sans-serif;">I hope this post makes it to other customers experiencing similar latency issues with applications that have WebView2.dll dependencies as we fixed quite a lot when we added the reg key.</span></p><p><br></p><p>Computer\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge</p><p>Add Key - WebView2</p><p>Add DWORD (32-bit) Value - QuicAllowed - 0x00000000</p><p><br></p><p><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/enterprise#browser-policies" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Enterprise management of WebView2 Runtimes - Microsoft Edge Developer documentation | Microsoft Learn</a> - Browser policies do not apply to WebView2</p><p><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Microsoft Edge Browser Policy Documentation | Microsoft Learn</a></p><p><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-webview-policies" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Microsoft Edge WebView2 Policy Documentation | Microsoft Learn</a></p><p><a href="https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/2507" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">How can you use browser policies within WebView2? · Issue #2507 · MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback (github.com)</a></p><p><a href="https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/2974" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Need support for Webview2 browser policies to enable Kerberos delegation · Issue #2974 · MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback (github.com)</a></p><p><br></p><p>Thanks!</p>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AZFzVTCQ1/how-to-allow-ssh-on-https-port-for-specific-domains-using-ztfw","lastmod":"2025-05-02T16:46:12.000Z","id":"0D54u0000AZFzVTCQ1"} -->
## How To: Allow SSH on HTTPS port for specific domains using ZTFW

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AZFzVTCQ1/how-to-allow-ssh-on-https-port-for-specific-domains-using-ztfw
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-07-27T02:16:42.000Z
- Last activity: 2025-05-02T16:46:12.000Z
- Answers: 3
- Likes: 3
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p>In this article we will see how you can use ZTFW to allow SSH traffic destined to HTTPS port (TCP 443) for specific domains only, while still blocking SSH traffic to HTTPS port for other domains.</p><p><br></p><p><strong>Pre-requisites</strong></p><p><br></p><p>1) Client machine with ZCC/Z-Tunnel 2.0 forwarding all DNS traffic to ZIA Cloud</p><p><br></p><p>In this setup we have a client machine with ZCC/Z-Tunnel2.0 with DNS resolver set to a public DNS resolver such as 8.8.8.8:</p><p><br></p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTJe?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>The DNS resolver is set to a public resolver (such as 8.8.8.8) to ensure that all DNS traffic is sent to ZIA Cloud.&nbsp;This is required because we will use a wildcard FQDN in our FW policy to match the domain for which SSH traffic should be allowed.</p><p><br></p><p>As documented at:&nbsp;<a rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-firewall-filtering-policy">https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-firewall-filtering-policy</a></p><p><br></p><p>To evaluate wildcard FQDNs against non-web traffic, Zscaler requires the IP address to which the FQDN resolves. Hence, for non-web traffic, the Zscaler service should be aware of the preceding DNS request/response. To ensure this, forward all of your DNS traffic to the Zscaler service if you intend to configure wildcard FQDNs in policies.</p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>2) Appropriate licenses</p><p><br></p><p>Here we will be using Advanced FW license.</p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><strong>Step-by-step guide</strong></p><p><br></p><p>1) Enable SSH tunneling under ATP</p><p><br></p><p>Go to Policy > Web > Security > Advanced Threat Protection:</p><p>Set SSH Tunneling to Allow:</p><p><br></p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTJo?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>2) Enable Enforce Firewall Control option for the location</p><p><br></p><p>If the location from where the user will access the ZIA Cloud is defined as a Location, make to enable the Enable Firewall Control option for that location.</p><p><br></p><p>Go to Administration > Resources > Traffic Forwarding > Location Management</p><p>Click on the location you want to add/edit and enable the Enforce Firewall Control option:</p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTJt?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>3) Configure FW policy</p><p><br></p><p>To configure a FW policy rule, go to Policy > Firewall > Access Control > Firewall Control.</p><p><br></p><p>Add the following two rules:</p><p><br></p><p>Rule: Add a FW policy rule to allow SSH traffic on HTTPS port for the wildcard FQDN</p><p>Network Service: HTTPS&nbsp;</p><p>Network Application: SSH</p><p>Destination: Wildcard FQDN: .github.com (Note the dot at the beginning of the FQDN).</p><p>Action: Allow</p><p><br></p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTKw?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTKD?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTLV?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>Rule: Add a FW policy rule to block SSH traffic on HTTPS port in general</p><p>Network Service: HTTPS</p><p>Network Application: SSH</p><p>Destination: Any</p><p>Action: Block/Reset</p><p><br></p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTLa?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTLf?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTLR?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>Here is a summary of the two rules:</p><p><br></p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTLk?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>Note:&nbsp;Make sure these two rules are above the Recommended Firewall Rule that allows all DNS/HTTP/HTTPS traffic as shown above.</p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>4) Activate the changes</p><p><br></p><p>Click on Activation > Activate to make the new changes take effect.&nbsp;</p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><strong>Verification</strong></p><p><br></p><p>Access the host ssh.github.com - it should get allowed as per our FW config:</p><p><br></p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTLz?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>Access a different SSH server on port 443 (here I had provisioned a custom SSH server listening on port 443 for testing purpose) - this should get blocked as per our FW config:</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwZwI?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p>Check the Firewall Insights logs:</p><p><br></p><p><img src="https://community.zscaler.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwTM9?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000iwZw3?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><strong>Important points to keep in mind</strong></p><p><br></p><p>In some case you may see the Action in the log message as "Allow due to insufficient app data". See the following Community article for details:</p><p><a rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evnDdCAI/when-allow-due-to-insufficient-app-data-log-entry-value-appears-and-when-it-does-not">https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evnDdCAI/when-allow-due-to-insufficient-app-data-log-entry-value-appears-and-when-it-does-not</a></p><p><br></p><p>In the above FW configuration rules, we paired matching on Network Application with another matching condition, Network Service. This is consistent with the recommended best practices as explained at:</p><p><a rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000A0dGk2CQE/best-practice-for-cfw-rules-with-network-application-dpi-detections-as-condition">https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000A0dGk2CQE/best-practice-for-cfw-rules-with-network-application-dpi-detections-as-condition</a></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AbTzr0CQC/sipa-forwarding-rule-options-with-standard-zero-trust-firewall","lastmod":"2024-09-25T16:56:33.000Z","id":"0D54u0000AbTzr0CQC"} -->
## SIPA forwarding rule options with Standard Zero Trust Firewall

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AbTzr0CQC/sipa-forwarding-rule-options-with-standard-zero-trust-firewall
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-09-09T18:40:39.000Z
- Last activity: 2024-09-25T16:56:33.000Z
- Answers: 4
- Likes: 4
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p><span style="font-size: 20px;">What is SIPA?</span></p><p><br></p><p>Traffic passing through the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange can egress any Zscaler IP address assigned to any given region in which a Zscaler data center is operating. This anonymizes the traffic in a sense where Zscaler is the source IP address for any given internet destination. The benefit is that "Company A" cannot be distinguished from Zscaler or any other Zscaler customer traffic. The disadvantage is only when certain destinations need to create ACL-based rules which depends on traffic to come from a consistent IP address that represents Company A and only Company A.</p><p><br></p><p>Source IP address Anchoring (SIPA) is a feature that allows egress from the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange from a customer-controlled IP address. This is done by effectively directing certain traffic from Customer A through an App Connector which is controlled by Customer A.</p><p><br></p><p>For more information about SIPA, please see the <a href="https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-source-ip-anchoring" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">SIPA Helpdocs</a>.</p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 20px;">Per-User Forwarding Needs Advanced Zero Trust Firewall</span></p><p><br></p><p>SIPA requires a Forwarding rule. Traffic forwarding is a function of the Firewall.</p><p><br></p><p>Standard Firewall includes the ability to define rules based on IP, port, protocol (L3/L4) and by FQDN or wildcard FQDNs including Forwarding rules. The Advanced Firewall brings several additional features but in terms of Forwarding rules it brings the ability to define a rule based on user, group, or department -- basically per-user rules supporting IdP integration.</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000izekH?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><strong>Most importantly: Without the Advanced Firewall, SIPA Forwarding rules cannot be created in a per-user basis and need to use the policy constructs available to the Standard Firewall</strong></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 20px;">Options for SIPA Forwarding Rules with Standard Firewall</span></p><p><br></p><p>The options for defining SIPA Forwarding rules using the policy constructs of the Standard Firewall include:</p><p><br></p><ol><li>Rule by source IP address.&nbsp;Where source means the private 10-space or similar assigned to customer users which are selected as a group or individually into a source IP group then referenced in the forwarding policy;</li><li>Rule by destination IP or FQDN.&nbsp;Customer creates either a dest IP object (like the source side above) or a Custom URL (careful, forwarding supports the full URL path and just the FQDN portion).&nbsp;Then reference these objects in Forwarding policy;</li><li>Rule by location or sublocation.&nbsp;Carve out the customer users into locations and reference these in Forwarding policy;</li><li>Rule by combining any/all of the above.&nbsp;These conditions are logically ANDed together and so all have to match (be "true") for the forwarding rule to hit.&nbsp;A customer Admin can get pretty tightly defined rules by specifying "any flow (from a source IP in 10.1.1.0/24) AND ((is going to example.com) or (2.2.2.2)) AND (is in sublocation3) forwards via SIPA".&nbsp;This is a good way to narrow down options 1, 2, or 3 if any one of them by themselves isn't narrow enough.</li></ol><p>Forward rule with Standard ZT Firewall</p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000izgUu?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000Ac6WyXCQU/how-to-block-rammerhead-interstellar-doge-etc-","lastmod":"2024-09-24T12:48:09.000Z","id":"0D54u0000Ac6WyXCQU"} -->
## How to Block Rammerhead, Interstellar, Doge etc ?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000Ac6WyXCQU/how-to-block-rammerhead-interstellar-doge-etc-
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-09-18T20:59:00.000Z
- Last activity: 2024-09-24T12:48:09.000Z
- Answers: 8
- Likes: 0
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p>Hello,</p><p><br></p><p>I would like to discuss an issue we’ve recently discovered and get your insights on how we can prevent it.</p><p><br></p><p>There are web-based applications on the internet that function as proxies. Some examples include Rammerhead, Interstellar, and Doge Network/Unblocker. These applications operate across thousands of domains, thanks to free DNS services. Below are a few examples along with their Zscaler categories:</p><p><br></p><p> • https://math.root.sx (Internet Services)</p><p> • https://sus.it.com (Corporate Marketing)</p><p> • https://agentchuck.manoahinvest.com (Finance)</p><p> • https://5lung.powergrass.ro (Health)</p><p><br></p><p>There are hundreds of URLs like these operating in almost every category, and you can find them with a bit of research online.</p><p><br></p><p>When you access these sites, they run a browser within a browser, allowing users to access websites they wouldn’t normally have permission to visit. They can also download files, etc., onto their devices using this proxy mechanism.</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jTnoi?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jTnnR?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p style="text-align: center;"><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jTnp2?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jTnos?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p>Yes, this issue can be addressed by using a custom URL category, but we need to use predefined URL categories for some departments, and these types of websites pose a risk for us. Is there a way to block this on Zscaler?</p><p><br></p><p>Thanks in advance.</p>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

## How-To: Translate Regular DNS Traffic to DoH using DNS Gateway

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AeXDjZCQW/howto-translate-regular-dns-traffic-to-doh-using-dns-gateway
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-11-22T22:54:34.000Z
- Last activity: 2024-11-29T09:27:55.000Z
- Answers: 2
- Likes: 2
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p><strong>References</strong></p><p><a rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-dns-gateways">https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-dns-gateways</a></p><p><a rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-dns-control">https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-dns-control</a></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><strong>Overview</strong></p><p><br></p><p>In this article we see how you can use&nbsp;DNS Gateway to translate regular DNS traffic (over UDP or TCP) to DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) and forward it to a DoH resolver.</p><p><br></p><p><strong>Note: </strong>Zscaler provides DNS resolution service through Zscaler Trusted Resolvers (ZTR)&nbsp;in more than 150 edge locations.&nbsp;Using DNS Control + ZTR you can eliminate the need to send DNS traffic to a 3rd party DNS resolver.</p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><img src="/zenith/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jxHRi?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><strong>Pre-requisites</strong></p><p><br></p><p>1) DoH Resolver</p><p>You should have a publicly accessible DoH resolver.&nbsp;Here we will use a custom DoH resolver that was setup for the purpose of this article.</p><p><br></p><p>2) Recommended Firewall Rules</p><p>Also make sure that the Recommended Firewall Rule rule to allow DNS, HTTP and HTTPS traffic is enabled, and that there is no higher ordered rule that would block DNS traffic:</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/zenith/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jxHID?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><strong>Step-by-step guide</strong></p><p><br></p><p>1) Enable Enforce Firewall Control option for the location</p><p>If the location from where the user will access the ZIA Cloud is defined as a Location, make to enable the Enable Firewall Control option for that location.</p><p><br></p><p>Go to&nbsp;Administration > Resources > Traffic Forwarding > Location Management</p><p>Click on the location you want to add/edit and enable the&nbsp;Enforce Firewall Control&nbsp;option as shown:</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/zenith/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jxHRY?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p>2) Add DNS Gateway</p><p>Go to&nbsp;Administration > Resources > Forwarding Methods > Proxies &amp; Gateways</p><p><br></p><p>Under the tab&nbsp;DNS Gateways: Click on Add DNS Gateway:</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/zenith/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jxHRO?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p>Specify values for the DNS Gateway as shown:</p><ul><li><strong>Name: </strong>e.g. DNSGW1.</li><li><strong>Protocol: </strong>DNS over HTTPS.</li><li><strong>Primary DNS Server: </strong>IP address or FQDN of the DoH service (e.g. doh.gs-tests.com).</li><li><strong>Failure behavior: </strong>The action to be performed when both primary and secondary resolvers are unavailable to serve the requests. Here we have chosen the option "Return Error Response".&nbsp;</li></ul><p><br></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jxHqn?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><strong>Note: </strong>Here we have just specified a primary DNS server, however as a best practice, you should specify both a primary and secondary DNS server.</p><p><br></p><p>Click on&nbsp;Save.&nbsp;The Gateway should now appear in the list of DNS Gateways.</p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>3) Add DNS Control rule to forward DNS traffic to this DoH Gateway:</p><p>Go to&nbsp;Policy > Firewall > Access Control > DNS Control</p><p><br></p><p>Then click on Add DNS Filtering Rule and add a new DNS Filtering rule as shown:</p><ul><li><strong>Rule Order: </strong>Make sure the rule is ordered high enough, before the default DNS rule to allow DNS traffic.&nbsp;Here we have set it to 1.</li><li><strong>Rule Name: </strong>e.g. Redirect to DoH.</li><li><strong>Rule Status: </strong>Enabled.</li><li><strong>Action: </strong>Redirect Request using DoH.</li><li><strong>DNS Gateway: </strong>DNSGW1.</li></ul><p><br></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jxHqs?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p>Click&nbsp;Save. The DNS Control rule will appear in the list.</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jxHqx?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>4) Activate changes</p><p>Click on&nbsp;Activation > Activate.</p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><strong>Verification</strong></p><p><br></p><p>Connect a client using ZCC/Z-Tunnel 2.0:</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/zenith/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jxHQ1?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p>Now initiate a regular DNS lookup. Specify a public resolver, such as 8.8.8.8, to ensure that DNS traffic is tunneled to ZIA Cloud.</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/zenith/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jxHPw?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p>To confirm that these DNS requests were translated to DoH and forwarded to our DoH resolver, check the DNS logs.&nbsp;</p><p>Go to&nbsp;Analytics > Insights > DNS Insights > Logs</p><p>Select the timeframe, say last 5 minutes, and click on Apply Filters:</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0684u00000jxHr7?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><strong>Additional References</strong></p><p>Zscaler DNS Security and Control Reference Architecture Guide: <a rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://help.zscaler.com/downloads/zia/reference-architecture/zscaler-dns-security-and-control-0/zscaler-dns-security-and-control-reference-architecture_0.pdf">https://help.zscaler.com/downloads/zia/reference-architecture/zscaler-dns-security-and-control-0/zscaler-dns-security-and-control-reference-architecture_0.pdf</a></p>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AfBBHDCQ4/enhancing-security-in-developer-environments-with-ssl-inspection","lastmod":"2025-11-18T03:19:23.000Z","id":"0D54u0000AfBBHDCQ4"} -->
## Enhancing Security in Developer Environments with SSL Inspection

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AfBBHDCQ4/enhancing-security-in-developer-environments-with-ssl-inspection
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-12-11T18:23:39.000Z
- Last activity: 2025-11-18T03:19:23.000Z
- Answers: 1
- Likes: 3
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p>Hello Zscaler Community,</p><p><br></p><p>We hear from many of you that you’re constantly balancing the need for robust security measures with the necessity to maintain a seamless software development workflow. One critical area where this balance is crucial is in the implementation of SSL/TLS inspection within developer environments.</p><p><br></p><p>Encrypted traffic inspection is a powerful tool in our security arsenal that provides the visibility necessary to block threats hidden within. However, setting it up in a way that doesn't disrupt developer productivity can be challenging. I'd like to share some insights and open up a discussion on how you can effectively implement SSL/TLS inspection without slowing down your developers.</p><p><br></p><p><strong>Key Steps for Implementing SSL Inspection</strong></p><p><br></p><p>Here are some high-level recommendations to think about as you consider implementing encrypted traffic inspection for your dev team:</p><p><br></p><ol><li><strong>Creating an SSL Inspection Policy:</strong> It's essential to configure policies that selectively bypass traffic associated with specific development tools while inspecting other types of traffic. This targeted approach helps minimize disruptions to developer workflows.</li><li><strong>Integration of Development Tools with Zscaler:</strong> Ensuring that all development tools are integrated with Zscaler's certificate store is crucial. Zscaler can support 20 different tools and programming languages for traffic inspection but without adding extra processes for developers to contend with.</li><li><strong>Automating Certificate Management:</strong> Automating the use of the correct certificate stores can significantly reduce the manual overhead for developers. This automation ensures that security is a background process, not a hurdle.</li><li><strong>Custom CA Bundles:</strong> Building a custom CA bundle that includes the Zscaler root certificate is vital. This ensures that all tools and applications within the development environment trust the intercepted traffic, thereby maintaining the integrity of the development process.</li><li><strong>Tool-Specific Configuration:</strong> Each tool might require specific steps to integrate with the SSL/TLS inspection process. For instance, configuring Oracle Java with the <span style="font-family: courier;">keytool</span> command or setting up Git to recognize the custom CA-bundle with <span style="font-family: courier;">git config --global http.sslCAInfo</span> are key to those specific tools.</li></ol><p><br></p><p>We have a blog that dives deep into this as well as a solution guide with practical examples that show you how to implement encrypted traffic inspection for many developer tools. There’s also valuable help documentation on this topic that covers how to put SSL inspection to work with specific developer tools.</p><p><br></p><p>We’d also love to get your “from the trenches” perspective on:</p><ul><li>How you’ve implemented SSL inspection in your environments, and what challenges have you faced.</li><li>The specific tools or programming languages that you find more challenging to configure for SSL inspection.</li><li>What strategies have you found effective in maintaining a balance between security and developer productivity?</li><li>How you solved problems with these special developer-favorite tools like ngrok or similar.</li></ul><p>Here are the resources:</p><ul><li>Blog: <a href="https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/product-insights/ssl-inspection-developer-environments-unlock-advanced-threat-protection" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Setting Up SSL Inspection in Developer Environments to Defend Against Advanced Threats</a></li><li><a href="https://customer.zscaler.com/software-developer-solution-guide" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Solution guide</a></li><li><a href="https://help.zscaler.com/unified/adding-custom-certificate-application-specific-trust-store" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Help files for adding custom app certificates</a></li></ul>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

## SSL Inspection - PKIX path building failed: sun.security.provider.certpath.SunCertPathBuilderException errors

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AfI1I2CQK/ssl-inspection-pkix-path-building-failed-sunsecurityprovidercertpathsuncertpathbuilderexception-errors
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2024-12-13T08:50:33.000Z
- Last activity: 2024-12-17T02:22:21.000Z
- Answers: 3
- Likes: 0
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p>Hello community:</p><p><br></p><p>After enabling SSL Inspection, we are running into these errors when connecting to an iPaaS application from the Linux server. The client application on Linux connects to its web hosted control plane (Example cdn.xxx.com). The java cacert truststore on Linux has already been updated with the complete chain of ZScaler root and intermediate certificates.</p><p><br></p><p><em style="font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 10.5pt;">PKIX path building failed: sun.security.provider.certpath.SunCertPathBuilderException: unable to find valid certification path to requested target]","exc</em></p><p><br></p><p>In addition, we also see a TLSv1.3 Client Hello (SNI cdn.xxx.com), followed by a TCP RST in the network tcp dump around the time of this failure.</p><p><br></p><p>The target platform does not support TLSv1.3, and the inspection policy has TLSv1.2 and above set so not sure why the TLSV1.3 Client Hello is showing up in the TCP Dump.</p><p><br></p><p>As a workaround, we have enabled an exception for the control plane host address (example: cdn.xxx.com)</p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 10.5pt;">Are there other steps to be performed on the web application side to resolve these connectivity issues? The control plane web application has a different root cert and does not have the ZScaler root certificate pinned.</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 10.5pt;">The exception cannot be kept in place for an extended period of time.</span></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 10.5pt;">Thanks</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 10.5pt;">RB</span></p>

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000RKAwd0AH/zscalers-one-click-for-microsoft-365","lastmod":"2025-06-27T00:31:47.000Z","id":"0D5PJ00000RKAwd0AH"} -->
## Zscaler's One Click for Microsoft 365

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000RKAwd0AH/zscalers-one-click-for-microsoft-365
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2025-01-22T01:06:27.000Z
- Last activity: 2025-06-27T00:31:47.000Z
- Answers: 3
- Likes: 5
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p><strong>Overview</strong></p><p>Microsoft 365 (M365) is a suite of cloud-based services designed to enhance security, reliability, and user productivity for organizations. It offers a comprehensive set of applications and services, updated automatically to ensure users always have the latest versions.</p><p><br></p><p>If your organization utilizes any M365 applications, you can seamlessly route all M365 traffic (including remote user traffic) through the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) to the Microsoft cloud.</p><p><br></p><p>Currently, Zscaler has two configuration options to choose from for Microsoft 365 traffic:</p><p><br></p><p><strong><em>Microsoft-Recommended One Click Office 365 Configuration</em></strong></p><p>In Experience Center: Under Policy > Access Control > Internet &amp; SaaS > Advanced Settings</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/068PJ00000MfiWg?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><strong><em>Office 365 One Click Configuration: </em></strong></p><p>In Experience Center: Under <strong><em> </em></strong>Policies > Common Configuration > Advanced > Advanced Settings</p><p><strong><em>﻿</em></strong></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/068PJ00000Mfftz?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p>In this article, we look at the "Microsoft-Recommended One Click Office 365 Configuration" since it is based on Microsoft's recommendations.</p><p><br></p><p>Microsoft recommends that proxies transparently forward end-user M365 traffic to their cloud. To facilitate this for security vendors like Zscaler, Microsoft provides a publicly available list of FQDNs, wildcard domain names, and IP address ranges for the endpoint set. Zscaler leverages this list to identify M365 application traffic based on IP address and FQDN.</p><p><br></p><p>Zscaler’s ‘One Click’ setting allows this traffic to be forwarded directly to the Microsoft cloud, bypassing SSL Inspection and other security policies for optimal performance.</p><p><br></p><p><strong><em>Note: </em></strong><em>While the One Click setting optimizes performance, Zscaler selectively inspects M365 traffic to prioritize security. This ensures that while performance is enhanced, your organization maintains a robust security posture. See more on this under Zscaler Philosophy: Selective Inspection.&nbsp;</em></p><p><br></p><p><strong>Data Sources and Updates</strong></p><p>Zscaler uses a select list of&nbsp;FQDNs and IP ranges listed in the following Microsoft 365 endpoint sources:</p><p><br></p><ul><li>Office 365 Worldwide (+GCC)</li><li>Office 365 operated by 21 Vianet</li><li>Office 365 U.S. Government DoD</li><li>Office 365 U.S. Government GCC High</li></ul><p><br></p><p>Zscaler regularly updates this information. Zscaler checks for updates every 24 hours and performs a complete update weekly to ensure comprehensive accuracy.</p><p><br></p><p><strong>Zscaler Philosophy: Selective Inspection</strong></p><p>While the One Click setting bypasses SSL Inspection for most M365 traffic, Zscaler may selectively inspect certain traffic to ensure robust security.</p><p><br></p><p>Zscaler conducts thorough security assessments of Microsoft’s recommendations. In cases where a recommendation may pose a security risk, Zscaler will prioritize customer security and may not include it in the default ‘allow’ in the One Click setting.</p><p><br></p><p>For example, at one Microsoft recommended allowing access to a broad range of Azure blobs (e.g., *.blob.core.windows.net). This was deemed to be a potential security risk by Zscaler ThreatLabz and so Zscaler did not include this in the One Click setting.</p><p><br></p><p><strong>Customization Options</strong></p><ul><li><strong>Bypass Specific Traffic: </strong>If you need to bypass SSL Inspection for any specific FQDN or URL (including general blob access), you can easily create a custom URL category and configure an SSL Inspection policy to exempt that category.</li><li><strong>Apply Inspection to M365 Traffic:</strong> If you determine that the One Click setting is too permissive for your specific security requirements, you can create an SSL Inspection policy to apply inspection to M365 traffic.</li></ul><p><br></p><p><strong>Key Benefits of Using Zscaler with Microsoft 365</strong></p><ul><li><strong>Enhanced Security:</strong> Zscaler's selective inspection approach ensures a strong security posture while optimizing performance for M365 applications.</li><li><strong>Comprehensive Visibility:</strong> Gain complete visibility into all user traffic, both Microsoft and non-Microsoft, through a single source of logs. Additionally, with Zscaler Client Connector's Flow Logging feature, one can get visibility into traffic that may be bypassed from the endpoint via ZCC, such as Microsoft Teams traffic.</li><li><strong>Selective Inspection: </strong>Maintain the ability to inspect all M365 traffic for selected services or during periods of heightened risk (e.g., during attacks or mergers).</li><li><strong>Bandwidth Control:</strong> Optimize network performance by controlling bandwidth for both Microsoft and non-Microsoft services.</li><li><strong>Global Network and Peering: </strong>Zscaler's global network with extensive peering with Microsoft ensures efficient and secure communication with the Microsoft cloud.</li><li><strong>Tenant Restrictions:</strong> Enhance data security and prevent data leakage by dividing personal and corporate Microsoft services and enforcing tenant restrictions.</li></ul><p><br></p><p><strong>References and Further Reading</strong></p><ul><li><a href="https://help.zscaler.com/unified/about-microsoft-one-click-options" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Zscaler Help documentation for M365/O365 (Experience Center)</a></li><li><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/urls-and-ip-address-ranges?view=o365-worldwide" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Microsoft 365 URLs and IP address ranges</a></li><li><a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/microsoft-365-network-connectivity-principles?view=o365-worldwide" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Microsoft 365 network connectivity principles</a></li><li><a href="https://www.zscaler.com/resources/white-papers/best-practices-for-microsoft365-and-zscaler.pdf" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Zscaler and Microsoft Best Practices Guide</a></li><li><a href="https://www.zscaler.com/partners/microsoft" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Zscaler and Microsoft partnership</a></li></ul>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000RMpFz0AL/copy-of-overlap-between-custom-url-category-and-authentication-exemptions","lastmod":"2025-01-24T10:26:43.000Z","id":"0D5PJ00000RMpFz0AL"} -->
## Copy of Overlap between custom URL category and authentication exemptions

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000RMpFz0AL/copy-of-overlap-between-custom-url-category-and-authentication-exemptions
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2025-01-22T18:35:55.000Z
- Last activity: 2025-01-24T10:26:43.000Z
- Answers: 1
- Likes: 3
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<ol><li><span style="font-size: 12pt;">When a URL is added to Exempted URLs under Authentication Exemptions on the Advanced Settings page, it is assigned to an internal URL category called Auth_Bypass, while the parent category is preserved.This URL category is not visible under Administration > URL Categories and cannot be selected in any policy rules because it is only used to bypass cookie-based authentication. You can only add or remove URLs from this category by adding or removing them from Authentication Exemptions. Read more about these exemptions </span><a href="https://help.zscaler.com/zia/exempting-urls-cloud-apps-authentication" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-size: 12pt;"><u>here</u></a><span style="font-size: 12pt;">. </span></li><li><span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Assume "xyz.safemarch.com" is added to the Authentication Exemptions URL list in Advanced settings. </span><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/068PJ00000GBsqI?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></li><li><span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">If you create a custom URL category and enter the wildcard domain for the aforementioned authentication-exempted URL in the URLs Retaining Parent Category field, the policy evaluation will treat it as a less specific match. Continuing from the previous example, suppose ".safemarch.com" has been added to the custom category CAT1, and the predefined URL category for this domain is Professional Services.</span><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/068PJ00000GBWwM?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></li><li><span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">When a user visits the website "xyz.safemarch.com," the categorization engine chooses the most specific category, in this case Auth_Bypass. Because no policy can be defined for this special URL category, the action taken will be determined solely by the policy for the predefined URL category for “xyz.safemarch.com”; any CAT1 rules will be ignored for this transaction. This logic of the most specific match is explained </span><a href="https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-url-categories" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"><u>here</u></a><span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">The logs would show the predefined URL category. In this case, “Professional services” will be displayed</span></li></ol><p> <img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/068PJ00000GBsoj?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><strong style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Solution:</strong></p><ol><li><span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"> On the Advanced Settings page, under Authentication Exemptions, add the URL "xyz.safemarch.com" to the Exempted URLs list.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Add "xyz.safemarch.com" to the URLs Retaining Parent Category field in URL category CAT1, along with ".safemarch.com". Create a URL filtering rule that allows the category CAT1. Create a second rule blocking the category Professional Services</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">Now, when you access "xyz.safemarch.com," both Auth_Bypass and CAT1 are equivalent. As a result, the transaction will be permitted in accordance with the policy for the custom category. In this case, CAT1 will be logged as the URL category in web insights.</span><span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 11.5pt;"> </span></li></ol>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

## Local FTP

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000eWfxc0AC/local-ftp
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2025-09-10T16:19:56.000Z
- Last activity: 2025-09-15T03:31:51.000Z
- Answers: 1
- Likes: 0
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p>We are rolling out Zscaler to our organization. In one of our offices, we have a Konica Minolta MFP. The MFP is setup to FTP scanned documents to a user's Windows Workstation. The Windows endpoints have a Windows program called "FTP Utility" installed on them to receive the scanned documents. The MFP and endpoints are on the same VLAN- no firewalls, switches, routers between them. Before Zscaler, everything worked fine. Once we installed Zscaler, the FTP functionality "broke." If we disable ZIA, the MFP scan send scanned documents to endpoints without issue. So something in ZIA is blocking INCOMING FTP from a local MFP. I have been working with support on this, but they have been unable to identify the cause. <p>Hello Team,</p><p>I would like to clarify my understanding regarding the concept of Certificate Chain Trust. My current assumption is that in order to successfully establish an SSL handshake, I need to trust the entire chain of certificates leading up to the root Certificate Authority (CA). This includes trusting the root CA itself as well as any intermediate CAs involved in the chain.</p><p><br></p><p>However, I have a question about how SSL inspection functions when dealing with short-lived issuing CAs. Specifically, these CAs have a validity period of only 14 days and are rotated every 7 days. Since these short-lived CAs are not permanently installed or trusted beforehand, I am curious about how SSL inspection manages to validate certificates issued by such transient CAs within this rapid rotation cycle.</p><p>Could someone please explain how trust is maintained in these scenarios and how SSL inspection handles the validation process with such short-lived CAs?</p><p>Thank you!</p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><img src="/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/068PJ00000TFDFZ?asPdf=false&amp;operationContext=CHATTER"></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p> </p>

## Antigravity & ZIA

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000uzLQn0AM/antigravity-zia
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2026-05-20T10:02:42.000Z
- Last activity: 2026-05-26T17:56:34.000Z
- Answers: 0
- Likes: 0
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p>Hello all,</p><p><br></p><p>Did anybody get Antigravity (incl. Login) to work, with ZIA running and without disabling SSL Inspections for .googleapis.com ?</p><p>I also looked into process based exceptions but this is a pain as well because of the way Antigravity is built. Zscaler support just told me to ask Google on what to bypass, Google says they don't support any SSL inspection for Antigravity.</p><p><br></p><p>Did anybody had any luck?</p><p><br></p><p>Thanks</p><p><br></p><p>edit:_________</p><p>It worked for us now with the newest version of Antigravity, the certificate just needs to be added to Node. Following the script we used:</p><p><br></p><p>#!/bin/zsh</p><p># Create file containing all macOS trusted root certs, plus Zscaler RootCA</p><p>security find-certificate -a -p /System/Library/Keychains/SystemRootCertificates.keychain > /Users/Shared/zscaler-for-developers/CAbundle.pem</p><p>cat /Users/Shared/zscaler-for-developers/ZscalerRootCA.pem >> /Users/Shared/zscaler-for-developers/CAbundle.pem</p><p><br></p><p># Set the NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS environment variable</p><p>echo 'export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/Users/Shared/zscaler-for-developers/CAbundle.pem' >> ~/.zshrc</p><p>source ~/.zshrc</p><p><br></p>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000w5mJD0AY/feature-request-http-header-profile-is-enabled-by-default","lastmod":"2026-06-15T15:41:29.000Z","id":"0D5PJ00000w5mJD0AY"} -->
## Feature Request - HTTP Header Profile is Enabled by Default

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D5PJ00000w5mJD0AY/feature-request-http-header-profile-is-enabled-by-default
- Type: Q&A
- Posted: 2026-06-08T03:04:20.000Z
- Last activity: 2026-06-15T15:41:29.000Z
- Answers: 1
- Likes: 0
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。
- Note: 回答本文は UI API では取得できないため未収録。

<p>Making a feature request here for HTTP Header Profiles to be enabled by DEFAULT and not a back-end feature flag request (<a href="https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-http-header-profile" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-http-header-profile</a>). From a partner perspective and having done many deployments, this feature request is almost always needed for improved fine-tuning of policies that adds flexibility in addressing edge cases. A common example is Windows Delivery Optimization traffic for Windows updates. This traffic is often IP-based and categorised as Miscellaneous by Zscaler. However, the User-Agent HTTP request header almost always contains the<em> Windows-Delivery-Optimization </em>User-Agent value. It's far more reliable and accurate to target this traffic via HTTP header profiles than using URL category keyword matching.</p><p><br></p><p>Additionally, Zscaler's major competitor, Netskope, offer HTTP Header Profiles out the box without any feature request required, saving deployment partners lots of time and providing the flexibility straight away to fine-tune policies. My ask is that this is enabled by default by Zscaler as I see no reason why additional time needs to be spent asking support to enable this backend flag.</p><p><br></p><p>Thanks,</p><p>Fraser</p>
<!-- /ZS-POST -->

---

<p>We've been a customer of Zscaler (ZIA) for ~8yrs now and love the product. <p>I’m looking for some help to resolve Microsoft URLs with Dedicated IP in combination with Microsoft's ip whitelisting function, called Conditional Access.</p><p><br></p><p>Just like Identity Proxy, you can NOT use Identity Proxy for Microsoft services IF your IDP is Entra. It’s the classic problem of trying to white list logging in, before you are authenticated.</p><p><br></p><p>Same problem with Dedicated IP. After we enter some Microsoft service URLs in the dedicated IP mechanism (in this case the Storage Browser service), it doesn’t work because we can’t authenticate first. We also our Zscaler dedicated IP entered into their Microsoft Conditional Access policy. We tested with one user by entering that user's outgoing Zscaler IP (from ip.zscaler.com) into the Microsoft Conditional Access policy, and it worked. So the theory of what's blocking is confirmed.</p><p><br></p><p>What this tells us is the Login Services are not getting through. The obvious solution is the start entering Login service URLs to the Dedicated IP ruleset, but I’ve tried this in the past and had conflicting results as the login URLs are a moving target.</p><p><br></p><p>So, my question is has somebody figured out a consistent approach to this? Thank you.</p>
